title: Stuttgart face big Europa League test in Fenerbahce 'hell' - NewsBreak
text:
By DPA ,
2 hours ago
VfB Stuttgart face a test of courage when they visit Fenerbahce and their partisan fans in Istanbul on Thursday in the Europa League.
“The fans here are really incredible, it’s something quite special. We’re also blessed with amazing fans, though. We’ll have to quickly acclimatise,” coach Sebastian Hoeness told reporters on Wednesday.
Fenerbahce fans are among the noisiest in the world, and Stuttgart's captain Atakan Karazor, who is of Turkish descent and has been called up into their national team, said he has also warned his team-mates what to expect.
"I asked a few players on the national team what it would be like here. They said it would be hell. And I passed that on to my team," Karazor said.
Hoeness meanwhile wants the team to deliver in "a really good challenge for us, which will ask everything of us. But that’s exactly what we want.
"We always try to utilise our intensity and will try to impress the opponents again tomorrow. On the one hand it’s tactical, on the other it’s a way of swinging the game in our favour,” he said.
Stuttgart have won their last four Bundesliga maatches but have had a mixed start in Europe, losing their last match 2-0 at Basel after an opening 2-1 victory against Celta Vigo.
Karazor may return into the starting 11 he has not always been part of lately, with Hoeness saying: "That is obvious to a certain extent, isn't it."
Karazor said: "My family will be in the stadium and obviously it’s a special match for me. The atmosphere and the match will stay with me. It’s special.”
